title: Planes and normal equations
section: Analytic Geometry of R3 ▷ Planes in 3-Space
terms: plane; normal equation; coordinate plane; parallel planes; angle between planes.

exposition.text:
A plane through P with nonzero normal n is n·(x −P ) = 0, or n x+ n y + n z = d. Its normal is
1 2 3
determined by the coefficients of the coordinates. Three noncollinear points determine a unique
plane; cross two independent displacement vectors to obtain its normal.
Parallel planes have proportional normals. The acute angle between two planes is the acute an-
gle between their normals, so use an absolute value in the cosine formula. A line lies in a plane
precisely when one of its points satisfies the plane equation and its direction is perpendicular to
the normal. The direction of the intersection of two nonparallel planes is their normals’ cross
product.
Planes with proportional normals coincide only when their constants have the same proportion-
ality factor; otherwise they are distinct parallel planes. For a whole family of plane equations,
equate coefficients of the free parameter to find points belonging to every plane.

question.text:
A plane contains the line r(t) = (1, 0, 1) + t(1, 2, 0) and the point (0, 1, 2). Which is its equation?
(A) 2x − y + 3z = 5 (B) 2x − y − 3z = −1
(C) x + 2y + z = 2 (D) x − 2y + 3z = 4
(E) 2x + y + 3z = 5

solution.text:
A second direction in the plane is (−1, 1, 1). Crossing (1, 2, 0) with it gives (2, −1, 3).
Evaluating at (1, 0, 1) gives constant 5.

question.text:
The planes x + y + z = 1 and x − y + 2z = 3 intersect in a line. Which vector is parallel to that
line?
(A) (−3, 1, −2) (B) (3, −1, −2) (C) (3, 1, −2) (D) (1, 3, −2) (E) (1, −3, 2)

solution.text:
Cross the normals: (1, 1, 1) × (1, −1, 2) = (3, −1, −2). Its dot product with each normal is
zero, so it gives the intersection direction.

question.text:
For which real a do the planes 2x − y + 2z = 3 and 4x − 2y + az = 12 have no common point?
(A) a = 0 (B) a = 2 (C) a = 4 (D) a = 6 (E) No real a

solution.text:
The normals are proportional only when a = 4, with ratio 2. In that case twice the first
plane equation has right side 6, inconsistent with 12, so the planes are distinct and parallel.
For every other a the normals are independent and the planes intersect in a line.

question.text:
What is the intersection of all planes λx + (λ − 1)y + z = 2λ + 1, where λ ranges over all real
numbers?
(A) The empty set
(B) The single point (2, 0, 1)
(C) The line (2 − t, t, 1 + t), t ∈ R
(D) The plane x + y + z = 3
(E) The line (2 + t, t, 1 − t), t ∈ R

solution.text:
Rearrange as λ(x + y − 2) + (−y + z − 1) = 0. For this to hold for every λ, both coefficients
must vanish: x +y = 2 and z −y = 1. Set y = t to obtain the displayed line. It satisfies every
member of the plane family.
